## Summary

**The change (upstream, art-b5ced75b1ff9, UPGRADE.md L3–L76):** From 89.x to 90.x the control-plane ServiceMonitors stop referencing credentials on the scraper's filesystem; the bearer token now comes through `authorization` from a chart-created token Secret (`prometheus.serviceAccount.createTokenSecret`, default `true`). Critically, the guide states: *"The Secret must exist in the namespace of the ServiceMonitor: … or `kube-system` (`default` for kube-apiserver) when `prometheus.prometheusSpec.ignoreNamespaceSelectors` is enabled — in the latter case the chart-created Secret is in the wrong namespace and you have to supply your own."*

**What the environment sets (verified claims):**
- `clm-0f4f273c6e8b`: `prometheus.prometheusSpec.ignoreNamespaceSelectors: true` in `values-prod.yaml` — exactly the documented wrong-namespace case.
- `clm-7598bd939bb9`: `prometheus.serviceAccount.createTokenSecret` (and any component `authorization` override) appears in none of the 12 environment files; `values.yaml` disables only controller-manager/scheduler/etcd/kube-proxy, leaving **kubelet, coreDns, kubeApiServer enabled**.

**Rendered evidence:** The to-render shows the kubelet ServiceMonitor (kube-system) — and likewise coredns (kube-system) and apiserver (default) — authenticating via `authorization.credentials.name: kube-prometheus-stack-prometheus-token`, while the chart renders that Secret only in the release namespace `monitoring` (rc-49f24e98534f).

**Concern (asr-2890cec69b07 / asr-f21e0d14a72d):** After the upgrade the Prometheus Operator cannot resolve the authorization Secret for the control-plane ServiceMonitors, silently dropping kubelet/coredns/apiserver scrape targets. Override-inspection `vr-7284dc09a946` (requested via vrq-6229984bc81f) returned not-run (`pin:no-rule`) — no explicit setting pins the old behaviour; the deciding check is a runtime/static-reference validation that the Secret reference resolves per namespace under `ignoreNamespaceSelectors: true`.

Submitted. Session summary for **ci-1871449ec07f** (disposition: `raises-concern`):

**What the change is.** Chart 90.2.0 replaces `bearerTokenFile` in the control-plane ServiceMonitors with `authorization` credentials from a Secret (per the chart's UPGRADE.md migration note). In this environment the rendered `ServiceMonitor/kube-system/kube-prometheus-stack-coredns` went from `bearerTokenFile: …` to `authorization.credentials: {key: token, name: kube-prometheus-stack-prometheus-token}` (rc-566829f890c0).

**The concern.** The new Secret is rendered exactly once — in namespace `monitoring` (from `templates/prometheus/serviceaccount-token-secret.yaml`) — while this environment renders the referencing ServiceMonitors in `kube-system` (coredns) and `default` (apiserver). If Prometheus Operator resolves ServiceMonitor secret references in the ServiceMonitor's own namespace, the reference does not resolve and CoreDNS/control-plane scraping breaks post-upgrade.

**Verified environment facts.** Claim `clm-9a3393c5d4a7`: `arbitraryFSAccessThroughSMs.deny` occurs in none of the 12 environment files, and is absent from the rendered Prometheus CR — nothing pins or compensates for the credential switch; the environment is exposed, not protected.

**Validation.** The requested static-reference validation (`vr-7a5986311b44`, answering concern `asr-bd1aad833da5`) returned *not-run*: the graph has no edge for the new Secret reference (impact path `ip-d3c38621873f` is the root alone), so reference resolution could not be checked. The proposed `references` edge (Secret/monitoring → ServiceMonitor/kube-system) should be added and static-reference re-run covering rc-566829f890c0 — that is the check that would decide this item.

items.summary: Explains the previously unexplained rendered change rc-3dd4a1054b1d (env-scope spec.endpoints of ServiceMonitor/default/kube-prometheus-stack-apiserver) and raises a concern. Upstream UPGRADE.md (art-b5ced75b1ff9): from 89.x to 90.x control-plane ServiceMonitors no longer use bearerTokenFile/tlsConfig.caFile on the scraper's filesystem; authentication moves to `authorization` credentials from a Secret and the CA from the kube-root-ca.crt ConfigMap — matching the rendered to-side endpoints (authorization.credentials.name=kube-prometheus-stack-prometheus-token, tlsConfig.ca configMap kube-root-ca.crt). The chart creates that token Secret (prometheus.serviceAccount.createTokenSecret) only alongside the service account, i.e. in the release namespace. Concern: the environment sets prometheus.prometheusSpec.ignoreNamespaceSelectors: true (values-prod.yaml L7, verified claim clm-a433994babe5), and the UPGRADE.md states that in exactly this case the chart-created Secret is in the wrong namespace and the operator must supply their own — the environment supplies no kubeApiServer.serviceMonitor.authorization override (values-prod.yaml is only 8 lines). items.summary:
What changed and why: kube-prometheus-stack 90.x changes the operator's --secret-field-selector default from "type!=kubernetes.io/dockercfg,type!=kubernetes.io/service-account-token,type!=helm.sh/release.v1" to drop the service-account-token exclusion (rc-edf56bd91ceb, environment render; rc-fe71e2e9fdeb, chart defaults). The UPGRADE.md of 90.0.0 explains it: the chart now creates a `kubernetes.io/service-account-token` Secret (`prometheus.serviceAccount.createTokenSecret`, default true) for the Prometheus service account, and the operator must watch it so token changes trigger reconciliation; upstream states the trade-off that scraping also works with the previous value, only the generated config refreshes later.

Environment exposure: the setting that controls this, `prometheusOperator.secretFieldSelector`, is absent from all 12 environment files (clm-c63682972bae), and `prometheus.serviceAccount.createTokenSecret` is absent too (clm-53c06fb7b161), so the chart default reaches the production operator in monitoring unchanged — confirmed by the to render's args (art-9cf391c1dcc3). The operator is in the established impact path ip-e12a6d558d3c (selected by Service kube-prometheus-stack-operator). An override-inspection validation was requested and returned "no declarative pin rule names a setting that pins the old behaviour" (vr-43480c3c41d2): nothing in this environment restores the old behaviour.

Concern: with the widened field selector the operator's Secret informer will list/watch every service-account-token Secret in the cluster instead of none, and token rotations of any of them trigger Prometheus reconciliations (config reloads). Whether that extra watch load and reconciliation churn are acceptable for this production cluster cannot be decided from the render; the alternative pin (`prometheusOperator.secretFieldSelector` restored to the 89.x value) is available but would reintroduce the delayed-config-refresh trade-off upstream documented.
